Sri Lankan Chicken Curry

45 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Simmering the Curry

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken thighs, bone-in, cut into pieces150g300g450g600g
Roasted curry powder1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Chili powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Salt (for marinade)¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Lime juice or vinegar (for marinade)5ml10ml15ml20ml
Vegetable oil10ml20ml30ml40ml
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves, minced1234
Ginger, minced½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Curry leaves6121824
Pandan leaf, knotted¼ piece½ piece¾ piece1 piece
Lemongrass stalk, bruised¼½¾1
Cinnamon stick¼½¾1
Cardamom pods1234
Whole cloves1234
Tomato, chopped30g60g90g120g
Water50ml100ml150ml200ml
Coconut milk100ml200ml300ml400ml
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp½ tsp

Steps

  1. In a bowl, toss the chicken with the roasted curry powder, chili powder, salt, and lime juice or vinegar. Let it marinate at room temperature for 20–30 minutes.
  2. Ask an adult to help warm the oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 4–5 minutes, until soft and starting to turn golden at the edges.
  3. Add the garlic and ginger and stir for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
  4. Add the curry leaves, pandan leaf, lemongrass, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, and cloves. Stir for 30 seconds to release their aroma.
  5. Add the marinated chicken and cook 4–5 minutes, turning the pieces, until the outside is no longer pink.
  6. Stir in the chopped tomato and cook 2 minutes, until it starts to break down.
  7. Pour in the water, season with the black pepper, cover, and simmer 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened and turned a deep reddish-brown.
  8. Stir in the coconut milk and simmer, uncovered, another 5 minutes — don't let it boil hard or the coconut milk can split.
  9. Taste and adjust salt. Fish out the lemongrass, pandan, and cinnamon stick before serving. Serve hot with rice.

Kottu Roti (Chopped Roti Stir-Fry with Chicken)

40 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Chopping Kottu on the Griddle

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Godamba roti or paratha (store-bought), torn into ribbons2 pieces4 pieces6 pieces8 pieces
Chicken breast or thigh, diced small100g200g300g400g
Vegetable oil15ml30ml45ml60ml
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Leek, sliced20g40g60g80g
Cabbage, shredded40g80g120g160g
Carrot, julienned20g40g60g80g
Garlic cloves, minced1234
Ginger, minced½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Curry leaves6121824
Roasted curry powder1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Chili powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Egg, beaten1234
Soy sauce5ml10ml15ml20ml
Lime wedges, to serve1234

Steps

  1. Stack the roti and slice them into thin ribbons with a knife or kitchen scissors. Set aside.
  2. Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a large flat pan or wok over medium-high heat. Add the onion, leek, garlic, ginger, and curry leaves. Cook 2–3 minutes, until fragrant and just starting to soften.
  3. Add the diced chicken, curry powder, chili powder, and salt. Cook 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until browned and cooked through with no pink left.
  4. Push everything to one side of the pan. Pour the beaten egg into the empty space and scramble for about 1 minute until just set, then mix it through the chicken.
  5. Add the shredded cabbage and carrot. Toss for 2 minutes, until just starting to wilt but still a little crisp.
  6. Add the torn roti ribbons and the soy sauce. Using two spatulas, chop and toss everything together vigorously for 4–5 minutes, breaking up any roti clumps, until the ribbons are evenly coated and some edges look lightly charred.
  7. Taste and add a little more salt or chili powder if needed.
  8. Pile onto plates and serve immediately with lime wedges to squeeze over the top.

Parippu (Red Lentil Dal Curry)

30 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Tempering the Spices

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Red lentils (masoor dal), rinsed60g120g180g240g
Water200ml400ml600ml800ml
Turmeric¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Onion, finely diced20g40g60g80g
Garlic cloves, minced1234
Green chili, slit½11½2
Coconut milk100ml200ml300ml400ml
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Coconut oil or vegetable oil (for tempering)10ml20ml30ml40ml
Mustard seeds¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Dried red chilies1234
Curry leaves (for tempering)5101520
Small red onion, thinly sliced (for tempering)10g20g30g40g
Fenugreek seedspinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp¼ tsp

Steps

  1. Put the rinsed lentils, water, turmeric, diced onion, garlic, and green chili in a pot. Ask an adult to help bring it to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
  2. Cook, stirring occasionally and skimming off any foam, for 15–18 minutes, until the lentils are fully soft and starting to break down into a thick curry.
  3. Stir in the coconut milk and salt. Simmer gently for 3–4 more minutes — don't let it boil hard once the coconut milk is in.
  4. While the dal finishes, make the tempering: warm the oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and cover loosely — they'll pop and sputter.
  5. Once the popping slows, add the dried red chilies, curry leaves, sliced red onion, and fenugreek seeds. Fry 1–2 minutes, until the onion is golden and the curry leaves are crisp.
  6. Pour the sizzling tempering straight over the finished dal — it should crackle audibly. Stir it in just before serving, or leave it pooled on top.
  7. Serve hot with rice or roti.

Fish Ambul Thiyal (Sour Sri Lankan Fish Curry)

40 minMediumServes 1–4

Prep — Fish Curry Simmering

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Firm white fish or tuna, cut into chunks150g300g450g600g
Goraka pieces, soaked (or 1 tsp tamarind paste per serving)2 pieces4 pieces6 pieces8 pieces
Warm water (to soak goraka)30ml60ml90ml120ml
Garlic cloves2468
Ginger, minced½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Black pepper, coarsely ground½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Chili powder½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Roasted curry powder½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Turmeric¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Curry leaves6121824
Pandan leaf, torn¼½¾1
Cinnamon stick¼½¾1
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Vegetable oil10ml20ml30ml40ml

Steps

  1. Soak the goraka pieces in the warm water for 10 minutes, then blend or pound them (with the soaking water) into a rough paste. If using tamarind paste, stir it with the same amount of warm water instead.
  2. Ask an adult to help pound or blend the garlic, ginger, black pepper, chili powder, curry powder, and turmeric into a thick paste. Combine with the goraka (or tamarind) paste.
  3. Rub the spice-and-sour paste all over the fish chunks in a bowl, coating every piece.
  4. Place the fish and any remaining paste into a heavy-bottomed pot in a single layer. Tuck in the curry leaves, pandan leaf, and cinnamon stick, and sprinkle over the salt.
  5. Drizzle the oil over the top. Do not add extra water — this curry is meant to be dry and thick, not soupy.
  6. Cover and cook over low heat for 20–25 minutes, gently shaking the pot occasionally instead of stirring, until the sauce has reduced to a thick, dark glaze and the fish is cooked through.
  7. Taste carefully — it should be intensely peppery, sour, and salty all at once. Serve warm with plain rice.

Devilled Chicken

30 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Stir-Frying with Peppers

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Chicken breast or boneless thigh, cut into strips150g300g450g600g
Cornstarch10g20g30g40g
Soy sauce (for marinade)5ml10ml15ml20ml
Salt (for marinade)pinch¼ tsp½ tsp½ tsp
Vegetable oil (for frying)30ml60ml90ml120ml
Onion, cut into petals30g60g90g120g
Green bell pepper, sliced30g60g90g120g
Tomato, cut into wedges30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves, minced1234
Ginger, minced½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Curry leaves5101520
Green chili, sliced½11½2
Chili flakes¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Soy sauce (for sauce)5ml10ml15ml20ml
Tomato ketchup15ml30ml45ml60ml
Black pepperpinch¼ tsp½ tsp½ tsp

Steps

  1. Toss the chicken strips with the cornstarch, soy sauce, and a pinch of salt until evenly coated.
  2. Ask an adult to help heat the oil in a wok or large pan over medium-high heat. Fry the chicken in batches for 4–5 minutes, until golden and crisp outside and cooked through with no pink inside. Drain on paper towels.
  3. Pour off all but about 1 tablespoon of oil. Add the onion petals, bell pepper, garlic, ginger, and curry leaves. Stir-fry 2–3 minutes, until just starting to char at the edges but still crisp.
  4. Add the tomato wedges, green chili, and chili flakes. Stir-fry 1 minute more.
  5. Stir in the soy sauce, tomato ketchup, and black pepper to make the sauce.
  6. Return the fried chicken to the pan and toss everything together for 1–2 minutes, until every piece is glossy and coated in the red-brown sauce.
  7. Serve hot, straight from the pan, with rice or bread.

Egg Hoppers (Appa) with Coconut Sambol

40 min (+1–2 hr batter rest)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Hoppers Fresh Off the Pan

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Rice flour60g120g180g240g
Coconut milk60ml120ml180ml240ml
Water40ml80ml120ml160ml
Instant yeast¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Sugar¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Salt (for batter)pinch¼ tsp½ tsp½ tsp
Eggs (for hoppers)1234
Salt & pepper (to season egg)pinch¼ tsp½ tsp½ tsp
Fresh or desiccated grated coconut (for sambol)30g60g90g120g
Red onion, finely chopped (for sambol)15g30g45g60g
Chili powder (for sambol)¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Lime juice (for sambol)5ml10ml15ml20ml
Salt (for sambol)pinch¼ tsp½ tsp½ tsp

Steps

  1. In a bowl, whisk the rice flour, coconut milk, water, yeast, sugar, and a pinch of salt into a smooth, thin batter (about the thickness of heavy cream).
  2. Cover and let the batter rest somewhere warm for 1–2 hours, until it looks a little bubbly and smells faintly fermented (traditionalists ferment overnight, but a shorter rest still works).
  3. While the batter rests, make the sambol: mix the grated coconut, chopped red onion, chili powder, lime juice, and a pinch of salt together in a bowl, rubbing it with your fingers so the flavors blend in. Set aside.
  4. Ask an adult to help heat a small, curved hopper pan (or small nonstick wok) over medium heat. Pour in a ladle of batter and quickly swirl the pan so it coats the sides thinly, leaving a pool of batter in the center.
  5. Crack an egg into the center of the batter. Season with a little salt and pepper.
  6. Cover with a lid and cook 3–4 minutes, until the edges turn golden and crisp and lift away from the pan on their own, and the egg white is set but the yolk is still soft.
  7. Carefully loosen the edges with a spatula and slide the hopper out onto a plate — it should hold its bowl shape.
  8. Repeat with the remaining batter and eggs. Serve hot with the coconut sambol spooned alongside.

Polos Curry (Green Jackfruit Curry)

35 minEasyServes 1–4

Prep — Cutting the Jackfruit

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Young green jackfruit (canned in brine, drained, or fresh), cut into chunks150g300g450g600g
Water (to boil jackfruit)200ml400ml600ml800ml
Turmeric¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Vegetable oil10ml20ml30ml40ml
Onion, sliced30g60g90g120g
Garlic cloves, minced1234
Ginger, minced½ tsp1 tsp1½ tsp2 tsp
Green chili, slit½11½2
Cinnamon stick¼½¾1
Curry leaves6121824
Roasted curry powder1 tsp2 tsp3 tsp4 tsp
Chili powder¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Coconut milk100ml200ml300ml400ml
Salt¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp

Steps

  1. Put the jackfruit chunks in a pot with the water and turmeric. Ask an adult to help bring it to a boil, then simmer 15–20 minutes, until fork-tender. Drain well.
  2. Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, ginger, green chili, cinnamon stick, and curry leaves. Cook 3–4 minutes, until the onion softens and everything smells fragrant.
  3. Stir in the curry powder and chili powder. Cook about 30 seconds, just until toasty-smelling.
  4. Add the boiled jackfruit and stir to coat it in the spices.
  5. Pour in the coconut milk and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook, uncovered, 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the curry thickens.
  6. Use the back of a spoon to lightly mash some of the jackfruit pieces against the side of the pot — this gives the curry its signature shredded texture while leaving some pieces whole.
  7. Taste and adjust the salt or chili. Remove the cinnamon stick before serving. Serve hot with rice or roti.

Watalappan (Bonus)

20 min (+35 min steam, +2 hr chill)EasyServes 1–4

Prep — Portioned and Set

Ingredients by Serving

Ingredient1234
Kithul jaggery or dark brown sugar, grated60g120g180g240g
Water (to melt jaggery)30ml60ml90ml120ml
Thick coconut milk150ml300ml450ml600ml
Eggs2468
Ground cardamom¼ tsp½ tsp¾ tsp1 tsp
Ground nutmegpinch⅛ tsp¼ tsp¼ tsp
Cashews, chopped10g20g30g40g

Steps

  1. Ask an adult to help warm the grated jaggery with the water in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until fully melted and smooth. Let it cool slightly.
  2. In a bowl, whisk the eggs until just combined.
  3. Whisk the coconut milk, cardamom, and nutmeg into the eggs.
  4. Slowly whisk in the cooled jaggery syrup until fully combined.
  5. Strain the mixture through a fine sieve into ramekins or a heatproof dish, to catch any lumps. Sprinkle the chopped cashews over the top.
  6. Set the ramekins in a steamer or a wider pan filled with an inch of hot water. Ask an adult to help cover and steam over medium-low heat for 30–35 minutes, until set around the edges but still gently wobbly in the center.
  7. Let the puddings cool to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving chilled.
